evidence.why: Both bring back your round-2 layout and change only the centre. The painted block won because it is the more ownable image — a square specimen whose red share is knocked out of the printed figure. The alternative is a calibrated progress gauge: slightly quicker to read, but closer to a familiar progress bar, which is what made round 3 feel regular.

system.why: Both return to the round-2 strata assembly. The chosen one plays the assembly by itself and lets you click a layer to light it — calm and clear. The alternative holds the screen and assembles one layer per scroll step on the homepage; it is more theatrical, but adds a pinned scroll you had found hard to follow last round.

handover.why: Both drop the dark side column and come in at under 1,000px. The chosen one keeps the six documents you approved in round 2 crossing the handover line. The alternative turns the handover into a dense ledger table on paper — the clearest to scan, but it gives up the drawn documents.

method.why: Both return to the family's instrument panel. The chosen one is your approved round-2 gantt, filled edge to edge, with a Kelwin's side → Handover → Yours axis along its foot. The alternative is a phase ledger with a compact gantt beside it — very legible, but it reads more like a project-management tool.
